judgments.rationale: Small teaser photo for the story about a man missing since 1998. The crop shows a road with an ambulance, parked cars, trees and low buildings (file name: King George Hospital near where his car was found). The alt, the headline, describes a man's disappearance, which the picture does not show, so claimTrue is yes. The img is not inside a link: it sits alone in the teaser's cover div, and the headline is a separate h3 inside an aria-labelled link right after it, so the alt is a word-for-word copy of the adjacent headline and says nothing about the picture. captureDiffers: the live HTML fetched on 2026-11-25 has the same teaser, img, src and alt, and the screenshot is the styled page with the same photo, so nothing that matters here differs. elementFails: my lean is yes. If the photo is informative, the alt does not convey what it shows (G94). If it only illustrates the teaser, it should be null (H67; F39 covers a non-null alt on an image that should be ignored). Either way, the headline copy is not a sufficient alternative. Label uncertain: competent auditors split on headline-as-alt for news teaser photos. Many treat it as acceptable because it identifies the story the picture belongs to, or only as a redundancy best-practice issue, not a 1.1.1 failure. Those who fail it also split on whether the defect is the one the claim names (alt does not describe the image) or a non-null alt on a decorative image. The rubric fixes no reading for this case.
